title: Radical nephroureterectomy with bladder cuff
subtitle: Kidney, whole ureter and a bladder cuff out in one piece, without opening the tract

sources.title: EAU Guidelines on Upper Urinary Tract Urothelial Carcinoma
BAUS procedure-specific patient information and consent guidance

indications: High-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma of the renal pelvis or ureter.
contraindications: Low-risk disease suitable for kidney-sparing treatment.
A solitary kidney or poor function where the patient would need dialysis (discuss alternatives).
preparation: CT urogram, ureteroscopy with biopsy and cytology, cystoscopy to exclude bladder tumour.
Renal function and the effect of losing the kidney on chemotherapy eligibility.
Consent: bleeding, conversion, urine leak from the cuff, bladder recurrence and the need for check cystoscopies.
positioning: Flank position for the kidney; repositioning or a lower incision for the distal ureter if needed.
equipment: Laparoscopic set, clips, vascular stapler, retrieval bag, catheter, fine absorbable sutures for the bladder.
anatomy: Renal artery and vein, the ureter along its length, its intramural part and orifice, gonadal vein, colon.
criticalSafety: Clip the ureter early, below the tumour, so cells do not drop into the bladder.
Never open the urinary tract; take the specimen out intact.
postop: Single intravesical chemotherapy instillation per guideline.

steps.emphasis: Biopsy and cytology, cystoscopy, renal function and the chemotherapy plan confirmed.
Flank position for the kidney; plan for the distal ureter (reposition or extend).
No entry into the collecting system or ureter at any point.
Fill the bladder and check the cuff closure.
Kidney, ureter and cuff in one bag, out intact, no morcellation.
Catheter until the cuff closure heals; cystogram first if needed.

step.nu.clip-ureter.title: Clip the ureter early
step.nu.clip-ureter.why: Clipping below the tumour before handling the kidney stops tumour cells being pushed into the bladder.
how: Find the ureter below the tumour early in the dissection.
Place a clip across it without dividing it.
Handle the kidney and ureter gently from then on.
pitfalls: Leaving the ureter open while the kidney is squeezed.

step.nu.hilum.title: Control the renal hilum, artery before vein
step.nu.hilum.why: Securing the artery first stops the kidney swelling with blood when the vein is closed.
how: Dissect the renal artery and vein at the hilum.
Clip or staple the artery and divide it; then staple the vein.
Check for accessory vessels against the CT.
pitfalls: Dividing the vein before the artery.

step.nu.kidney.title: Free the kidney outside Gerota's fascia
step.nu.kidney.why: The kidney, perinephric fat and ureter come out as one oncological block.
how: Free the kidney outside Gerota's fascia, taking the adrenal only if involved.
Follow the ureter down to the bladder, keeping it intact.
pitfalls: Breaching Gerota's fascia over the tumour.

step.nu.bladder-cuff.title: Excise the bladder cuff
step.nu.bladder-cuff.why: The intramural ureter and its orifice can carry tumour. Taking a cuff of bladder around it removes it and lowers local recurrence.
how: Free the ureter down into the bladder wall, tenting it up.
Excise a cuff of bladder around the orifice (extravesically, or opened under vision), keeping clear of the other orifice.
Close the bladder in two layers with absorbable suture.

step.nu.instillation.title: Single intravesical chemotherapy instillation
step.nu.instillation.why: One dose of chemotherapy into the bladder after surgery reduces the chance of a bladder recurrence.
how: Check the bladder closure is watertight and there is no suspicion of leak.
Give a single instillation (for example mitomycin C) per protocol, timed as the local guideline says.
Record it; follow cytotoxic handling rules.
pitfalls: Instilling into a bladder that may leak.
